text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- The EMU project is drifting from its original aim and the EMU criteria are fulfilled by trickery, said the Centre Party at its conference in Kokkola.
- The air in Helsinki is more polluted than hed been thought, study shows.
- Minister of Defence Anneli Taina offered courses in international military observation to the Chinese. @
Former finance minister Pohjola CEO Iiro Viinanen will need all his political experience to win backing for the company's planned reshuffle, to incorporate Suomi Salama.
KAUPPALEHTI
- List of items in the next round of pay talks (TUPO) will be long and principal questions should be resolved by summer.
- Producers of long fibre pulp expect its price to rise.
- Strong rise in apartment prices has diminished profits in investing in apartments. @
- Working group preparing restructuring of Suomi-Salama in Pohjola has not reached consensus over what the board of Suomi should decide.
AAMULEHTI
- New criminal procedures will be implemented in Finnish lower courts presumably next autumn, says Parliament's law committee head Henrik Lax.
- Closing down garrisons hinders development of voluntary defence work, says Alpo Saari, head of Finnish Reservists' Confederation. @
TURUN SANOMAT
- Success in the next round of pay talks (TUPO) depends on restructuring and development of working conditions; agreement on salaries and tax is not enough anymore, trade unionists say.
- Finland will keep demanding its own commissioner in the European Commission in the future, says Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen.
- Finance Ministry's state secretary Raimo Sailas wonders when there will be a political debate on the welfare state's future. @
- Green Party has turned 'nature' into a museum, the Centre Party says.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
